items.title: Numerical Analysis Applications in Improving Engineering Models
items.abstract: Numerical analysis serves as the fundamental pillar of modern engineering modeling, providing the mathematical and computational tools necessary to transform complex physical equations into practical numerical solutions. This study reviews contemporary applications of numerical analysis in enhancing engineering models, focusing on methodological advancements in solving partial differential equations, data-driven model order reduction techniques, adaptive mesh methods, and machine learning-based surrogate models. The study employs a synthetic analytical approach that combines a review of recent literature with an analysis of empirical results from various numerical methods, addressing hybrid models that integrate traditional techniques with artificial intelligence. The analysis demonstrates that combining traditional numerical analysis methods with artificial intelligence and reduced-order models has revolutionized the ability of engineers to simulate complex multiphysics systems with unprecedented accuracy and computational efficiency; hybrid models have achieved computational speedups ranging from 72 to 522 times compare to traditional methods. Furthermore, the study addresses challenges related to computational cost and solution sensitivity to initial conditions, examining cutting-edge innovative solutions such as physicsinformed neural networks and causality-based learning. The study concludes that future trends in this field are shifting towards the development of hybrid models that combine analytical accuracy with computational speed, with an increasing emphasis on generalization capabilities beyond the training data. This opens up broad prospects for digital engineering and digital twin applications across the industrial, energy, and infrastructure sectors. The study offers a comprehensive perspective on the development of engineering models using advanced numerical analysis techniques and identifies promising future research directions in this vital field.

items.title: Occupational risk profiles among public officials in Korea: A survey-based application of a first-tier risk assessment tool
items.abstract: Public officials perform diverse administrative, public-facing, emergency, and safety–critical tasks, yet their occupational risk profiles have rarely been characterized across actual job functions. In Korea, public officials have historically remained partly outside core occupational safety and health requirements, and systematic evidence on their occupational risk profiles across diverse job functions has been limited. This study applied the Public Officials’ Occupational Risk Assessment (PORA) tool to 36,779 Korean public officials to screen perceived occupational risks and identify occupation- and job-function-specific high-risk patterns. Respondents assessed exposure frequency and intensity for 24 occupational risk factors across psychological, organizational, ergonomic, physical, chemical, and biological domains. Risk scores were calculated as the product of frequency and intensity, and high-risk responses were defined as “high” or “very high” according to the PORA risk matrix. Prolonged sitting showed the highest mean risk score and high-risk prevalence, followed by public-facing work, fast work pace, time pressure, emotional stress, awkward posture, and repetitive upper-limb work. Frequency–intensity comparisons showed that some risks were driven by frequent exposure, whereas event-based psychological hazards received lower time-proportion-based frequency ratings but relatively higher intensity ratings. Occupation-specific logistic regression showed distinct profiles: general service officials were characterized by prolonged sitting and time pressure, police officers by broad psychological, ergonomic, and physical hazards, and firefighters by physical, chemical, biological, and emergency-response-related hazards. Job-function heatmaps and hierarchical clustering further revealed heterogeneous risk profiles across 22 main job functions. These findings highlight the need for job-function-based, participatory, and risk-prioritized occupational safety and health management in public organizations.

items.title: Omni-UBench: Benchmarking Omni-Modal LLM-based Guardrails Across Safety, Utility, and Reliability
items.abstract: Advances in Omni-modal Large Language Models (OLLMs) have enabled increasingly seamless human-AI interaction, but their unified processing of heterogeneous modalities also expands the attack surface, allowing adversaries to exploit richer input compositions to circumvent safety alignment. To counter such risks, omni-modal guardrails have been proposed to detect and filter unsafe queries across arbitrary modalities. However, their capabilities and limitations remain insufficiently understood due to the absence of a comprehensive evaluation benchmark. In this paper, we present Omni-UBench, the first comprehensive framework for omni-modal safety assessment, evaluating guardrail models along three critical dimensions, i.e., safety, utility, and reliability. Omni-UBench curates over 183k samples drawn from 35+ heterogeneous sources spanning text, image, audio, video, and their cross-modal combinations, annotated with safety labels under a unified risk taxonomy. Benchmarking under Omni-UBench on 15 representative OLLMs and omni-modal guardrails yields several key findings, including: (1) modern OLLMs exhibit strong content moderation potential even without guardrail-specific tuning; (2) existing guardrails still struggle to identify cross-modal queries that conceal harmful intent or involve sophisticated jailbreaks; (3) they further exhibit substantial safety hallucination and over-sensitivity to textual patterns, revealing a deficient understanding of cross-modal safety semantics. Our findings provide valuable insights for developing more trustworthy omni-modal guardrails in future research.

items.title: OneLatent: Latent Reasoning for Efficient Foundation Recommendation Models
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong reasoning capabilities, motivating their use as the backbone of foundation recommendation models (FRMs). Existing methods enhance recommendations through explicit Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning under a Think-then-Answer paradigm. However, explicit CoT incurs substantial inference overhead by generating lengthy reasoning traces and relies on manually designed templates that struggle to capture diverse, dynamic user interests. We propose OneLatent, an efficient latent reasoning framework that compresses explicit reasoning traces into several learnable latent tokens, enabling Latent-Reason-then-Answer inference without generating verbose traces. OneLatent first introduces Multi-View Adaptive CoT (MV-ACoT), which creates diverse, high-quality teacher-generated supervision by exploring user interests from multiple perspectives and automatically adapting reasoning complexity to each instance. Building on pretrained FRMs, it then uses a three-stage latent-token alignment paradigm to progressively internalize CoT traces into learnable latent tokens. Finally, a multistage curriculum-based post-training strategy activates latent-token reasoning for downstream recommendation tasks. Experiments on an industrial-scale Kuaishou dataset and the public Kuaishou LLM-Rec benchmark show that OneLatent consistently outperforms explicit CoT-based methods and traditional baselines. Compared with the Think and No-Think variants of FRMs, OneLatent improves SID@64 by 17.44% and 9.33%, respectively, while achieving over 17x higher online inference throughput. We further develop a production serving system for scalable, real-time FRM inference. An online A/B test in Kuaishou's local-services advertising scenario shows that deploying OneLatent with this system yields an estimated 9.6% revenue lift over strong online baselines, including OneRec and OneReason.

items.title: OpenDVP: an experimental and computational framework for community-empowered deep visual proteomics
items.abstract: Abstract Deep visual proteomics (DVP) is an emerging approach for cell-type-specific and spatially resolved proteomics. However, its broad adoption has been constrained by the lack of an open-source end-to-end workflow within a community-driven ecosystem. Here we introduce openDVP, an experimental and computational framework for accessible and scalable DVP. OpenDVP combines open-source image analysis tools (MCMICRO, QuPath and napari) with scverse formats (AnnData and SpatialData) for multiomics integration. It provides two workflows: a fast-track pipeline requiring no image analysis expertise, and an artificial intelligence-powered pipeline incorporating state-of-the-art methods for image preprocessing, segmentation and spatial analysis. We apply openDVP across three archival tissue studies (human placenta, early stage lung cancer and locally relapsed breast cancer), integrating spatial single-cell phenotypes with exploratory proteomic measurements. Finally, we introduce deep proteomic profiling of cellular neighborhoods as a scalable approach for spatial discovery proteomics.

items.title: Optical and Photonic Computing for Deep Learning Acceleration: Silicon Photonics, Mach-Zehnder Meshes, and Wavelength-Division Multiplexing
items.abstract: The relentless exponential scaling of foundation models and transformer architectures has pushed conventional silicon complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) digital accelerators (GPUs, TPUs) toward fundamental thermodynamic and interconnect boundaries. Joule heating, resistance-capacitance (RC) interconnect delay scaling, and the 'memory wall' severely constrain energy efficiency and compute density. Optical Computing and Integrated Silicon Photonics (SiPh) establish an analog non-Von Neumann hardware paradigm that executes fundamental linear algebra operations—specifically General Matrix-Matrix Multiplication (GEMM)—at the speed of light with near-zero runtime energy dissipation. By encoding vector-matrix activations into coherent optical wave fields and modulating light through cascaded Mach-Zehnder Interferometer (MZI) meshes, Micro-Ring Resonator (MRR) banks, and Wavelength-Division Multiplexing (WDM) waveguides, photonic tensor processing units (PTPUs) execute analog matrix multiplications in continuous time with sub-nanosecond propagation latencies. However, translating integrated photonic circuits into production deep learning accelerators introduces profound optoelectronic engineering bottlenecks: analog noise accumulation across deep optical meshes, severe thermal phase drift, limited electro-optic Digital-to-Analog / Analog-to-Digital (DAC/ADC) conversion resolution, non-linear activation implementation hurdles, and wafer-scale optical footprint scaling. This paper delivers an exhaustive, mathematically formal technical investigation and empirical benchmark of integrated photonic computing for deep neural network acceleration. We formalize the Clements and Reck unitary matrix decomposition algorithms over reconfigurable MZI topologies, derive the optical transmission transfer matrix under optical carrier phase error perturbations, and establish energy-per-MAC physical thermodynamic bounds across electro-optic conversion interfaces. Furthermore, we construct an empirical co-simulation and hardware testbed benchmarking silicon photonic meshes against state-of-the-art CMOS accelerators (NVIDIA H100, Google TPU v5p) across vision transformers, large language model attention heads, and resonant graph convolutions. Our empirical findings demonstrate that a 64x64 integrated MZI photonic mesh achieves a 58.4x improvement in energy-delay product (EDP) over 4nm digital CMOS cores, sustaining up to 128 Tera-Operations per Second per Watt (TOPS/W) at 4-bit to 8-bit equivalent precision, while active thermo-optic phase stabilization preserves 98.2% baseline classification accuracy. Finally, we establish open research directions in all-optical non-linear activation functions, co-packaged optical memory architectures, and wafer-scale photonic interconnect scaling.

items.title: Organisational support for evidence-based practice in occupational health services in Finland
items.abstract: There is very little published research about evidence-based practice (EBP) in occupational health services (OHS), and none to date in Finland. The Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) model of evidence-based healthcare provides a clear and intuitive conceptual framework for exploring how research evidence and the practice of medicine could be better integrated. Thus far it has seen very little use within the occupational health arena. This study explores the extent of organisational support given to OHS professionals in providing EBP in Finland. We collected survey data ( n = 524) from Finnish OHS physicians and nurses involved either solely in patient care duties or also in a managerial, development or expert role, using a validated online questionnaire (EBP-OHS) that was made available in two waves: in November 2020 and August 2021. We analysed quantitative data using descriptive methods and qualitative data using content analysis. Most respondents reported that their organisations value evidence-based practice (83%) and encourage staff to use evidence-based information (74%). In their opinion, the most important means to support EBP were managerial support and example, employee training, and a dedicated team or expert responsible for ensuring that care delivery consistently aligns with the latest evidence. The respondents wanted clear and uniform processes for implementing research evidence into practice, and IT systems that support both the implementation and reporting of EBP in practice. Successful EBP in OHS seems likely to require managers to set a good example, both in their attitude and actions. Building a culture of implementing EBP requires staff to be empowered to share and keep up with robust and relevant new evidence and to be allocated sufficient time to do so. OHS units need to have clear structures and forums dedicated to engaging in EBP. OHS would likely benefit from having clear implementation processes and EBP tools that allow systematic follow-up and reporting.

items.title: Organized and self-organized football activity and motivational regulation among boys and girls in a Norwegian youth talent pathway: A descriptive cross-sectional study
items.abstract: In talent pathways that formally include both sexes, it remains unclear whether boys and girls selected into the same pathway accumulate comparable football activity. This study aimed to (1) describe sex-stratified self-reported weekly football exposure and motivational regulation among 103 players (51 girls, 52 boys; 13.8 ± 0.9 years) selected for one regional division of a Norwegian national youth talent development program, and (2) describe age-cohort patterns across the ≤13-, 14- and 15-year cohorts. Players reported weekly football hours and sessions during the preparation period and competitive season. Because the dataset lacked club- and training-group identifiers, observations could not be assumed independent; the study is therefore descriptive and exploratory: sex-stratified exposure and motivational regulation are summarized as median [interquartile range, IQR], age-cohort exposure as mean ± SD, and between-sex patterns as differences in central tendency rather than as hypothesis tests. In this sample, boys reported higher total weekly football exposure than girls (median 10.8 vs. 7.0 h), with a proportionally larger difference for self-organized than organized activity. Boys reported slightly higher intrinsic motivation and identified regulation, whereas girls reported slightly higher amotivation, external regulation and introjected regulation; these differences were small relative to the scale range, and both groups reported high intrinsic motivation and low amotivation in absolute terms. Because players were drawn from shared but unmodeled development environments in a cross-sectional design, the findings are descriptive only: equal formal selection did not coincide with equal football exposure, particularly in self-organized activity, generating hypotheses for future cluster-aware studies.

items.title: PAIR: Preference-Aligned Intent Retrieval for Premium People Recommendation at LinkedIn
items.abstract: General-purpose embeddings trained on profile similarity often misrank candidates in professional networks, where relevance is inherently complementary rather than symmetric. For example, job seekers usually engage with recruiters rather than peers with similar credentials. Current user recommendation systems are often built on profile similarity or social signals such as shared connections, which are effective in friend-oriented social networks where users tend to connect with similar people or within existing social circles. However, this does not hold in professional platforms like LinkedIn, where interactions are often goal-driven and cross-role interactions, requiring matching based on complementary intents rather than similarity or social proximity. In this paper, we propose Preference-Aligned Intent Retrieval, a retrieval framework that is designed to model user intent preference instead of profile similarity. Our approach is inspired by the preference-learning perspective of Direct Preference Optimization, but instantiates preference learning as an exposure-conditioned multi-negative contrastive objective over embeddings. This formulation simplifies training and scales efficiently to large candidate sets without requiring an explicit reference model. Furthermore, we incorporate user interaction history by aggregating click histories with positional encoding to capture temporal order, which enables constant-cost updates of user representations over a fixed history window, allowing new interactions to be incorporated without re-encoding history. As a result, personalization can be updated efficiently using lightweight CPU operations without repeated LLM inference during serving. We evaluate PAIR on LinkedIn's Premium retrieval task. A 0.6B parameter model achieves a MAR@100 of 0.45.

items.title: Parameter-Efficient Adaptation of Large Language Models to a Low-Resource Agglutinative Language: A Corpus, Datasets, and a Reproducible Benchmark for the Bashkir Language
items.abstract: Bashkir is a low-resource agglutinative language written in Cyrillic and remains poorly represented in modern LLMs. We present an open resource suite and a systematic benchmark of adaptation methods: the Bashkir Web Corpus (71,567 documents, 46.9M tokens, 16 sources) and three labelled datasets for binary, multiclass and multilabel text classification; the benchmark covers the first two. Experiments use eight architectures (82M-8B: DistilGPT2, GPT-2 base/medium, Phi-3-mini, Mistral-7B, YandexGPT-5-Lite-8B, mBERT, XLM-R) and three adaptation groups (full fine-tuning, QLoRA, in-context learning), plus continual pretraining (CPT). (1) QLoRA on 3.8-8B models outperforms encoder-only fine-tuning on binary classification: YandexGPT-5-Lite-8B with CPT reaches macro-F1 0.748 vs 0.653 (XLM-R) and 0.650 (mBERT); pairwise differences are significant after Holm correction (p<0.001). (2) YandexGPT-5-Lite-8B significantly outperforms Mistral-7B and Phi-3-mini on multiclass classification, BPB and native-speaker ratings (mean 3.28 vs 2.52 and 2.22; n=100; alpha=0.69-0.77; p<0.05); on binary classification its QLoRA advantage is not significant (p>=0.084). (3) CPT effects depend on model and task: perplexity improves for Phi-3-mini (+0.58) and YandexGPT-5-Lite-8B (+0.33) but worsens for Mistral-7B (-1.15, p<0.001); on binary classification CPT helps Mistral-7B most (+4.0 macro-F1). (4) Tokeniser fertility on Bashkir varies 2.67x (2.92-7.80) and tracks adaptation quality, while perplexity across tokenisers is not comparable. Cyrillic tokenisers with Russian pretraining are preferable; LLM judges reproduce native ratings for grammar and coherence (rho=0.33-0.46) but not language correctness (rho=0.16, p=0.11); native evaluation remains necessary. All artefacts are open-licensed.

items.title: Passing the Wrong Test: Model Size and Discriminant Validity in LLM-Based Psychological Assessment
items.abstract: Validation studies of zero-shot language-model scoring of psychological interviews often rely primarily on a single convergent correlation with a questionnaire to establish validity. However, a bivariate correlation cannot reveal whether a model lacks discriminant validity, agrees poorly in absolute terms, produces non-random missing scores, or scores inconsistently. We evaluated eight open-weight families (1–70B active parameters) and eight commercial frontier models. The models scored the same sets of clinical interviews (Study 1: suicide recovery, n = 149; Study 2: future self-continuity, n = 164) across 52 configurations. Convergent validity improves with model size in both studies. However, the standard open-weight models tested achieve only about three-quarters of frontier convergent validity, with 11-fold greater mean absolute bias, more format failures, and lower repeatability in Study 1. In Study 2, standard open models (≤ 27B) are as strongly correlated with a closely related construct (suicide recovery) as with the target (mean difference −0.014), although they correlate less strongly with a distal neighbor (life satisfaction). All six frontier generations correlate more strongly with the target than with either neighbor (mean difference from recovery +0.117). On a local workstation, Gemma 4 31B is within the frontier range on all discriminant validity indices, outperforming its similar-sized predecessor. Llama 3.3 70B shows no greater discriminant validity than Gemma 4 31B, suggesting that discriminant validity is a function of release, not parameter count alone. Based on these findings, we suggest a minimum validation standard across five domains.

items.title: Patch Management or Public Law? A Critical Comment on the Five Eyes Guidance for the Careful Adoption of Agentic AI Services
items.abstract: On 1 May 2026, six Five Eyes cybersecurity agencies jointly issued Careful Adoption of Agentic AI Services, the first coordinated Anglophone statement on the governance of LLM-based autonomous agents. This Comment argues that, although the Guidance offers competent cybersecurity risk management within its stated remit, its institutional weight invites a broader governance reading that the document cannot bear, and that five structural limitations then come into view. First, the cybersecurity doctrines on which it relies are necessary but insufficient for agentic systems, whose delegated authority, underspecified goals, and long-horizon autonomy strain the assumptions of conventional controls. Second, it privatises systemic risk by imposing duties on deployers without specifying public-law obligations, redress, or liability across the agentic value chain. Third, it prescribes human oversight without specifying the conditions of effective control, so that responsibility risks being assigned to reviewers who lack the information, authority, or time to exercise it. Fourth, it reduces accountability to auditability, confusing a technical property with a legal relation between duty-holders and affected parties. Fifth, the security-defined mandates of its six authoring agencies, and the intelligence-oversight structures within which most of them sit, raise questions of institutional voice, while its Five Eyes-only authorship raises a risk of divergence from the AI frameworks now emerging in the European Union, the Republic of Korea and Japan. The Comment concludes by outlining the elements of an enforceable, rights-protective, cross-jurisdictional legal regime that should supplement, rather than be displaced by, the technical controls the Guidance recommends.

items.title: Patient Perception and Trust in Artificial Intelligence in Dental Care: A Systematic Review
items.abstract: Background: Patient trust may determine whether artificial intelligence (AI) is accepted in dental care, particularly when AI contributes to diagnosis or treatment planning. We aimed to synthesize patient-reported trust, confidence, acceptance, and preferences regarding dental AI and to identify factors associated with these outcomes. Methods: PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from database inception to 2 June 2026. Two reviewers independently screened records and extracted data. Risk of bias was assessed with the revised JBI tool for analytical cross-sectional studies. Because outcomes and metrics were heterogeneous, findings were synthesized narratively. The review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261439049). Results: The final synthesis included eight studies comprising 3171 participants from five countries. Attitudes were generally favourable when AI supported rather than replaced dentists. In one study, 47.7% accepted AI-assisted interpretation of diagnostic data, whereas 10.8% trusted an entirely AI-generated diagnosis. Another study found that 84.9% supported AI analysis of dental images followed by dentist review. A fixed-order vignette study improved lesion recognition but did not significantly change trust in the dentist. Interpretation was limited by non-probability sampling, heterogeneous and often non-validated measures, incomplete control of confounding, and reporting inconsistencies. Conclusions: Available evidence suggests conditional acceptance of dental AI, particularly when dentists retain oversight. Confidence in the prevalence estimates of trust and acceptance is low; these findings do not establish that AI improves trust. More representative studies using validated, conceptually distinct outcome measures are required.

items.title: Patterns of Artificial Intelligence Use Among Lower-Secondary Teachers Across Education Systems
items.abstract: Abstract Background: Research on teachers' AI use has largely focused on whether teachers use AI or how many purposes they report. These measures cannot show how teachers combine AI across different parts of instructional work or whether professional learning relates differently to those combinations. Objectives: This study identified patterns of professional AI use among lower-secondary teachers and examined whether AI-related professional learning differed across them. Methods: We analysed 2024 Teaching and Learning International Survey (TALIS) data from 25,705 teachers in 54 education systems who reported using AI for teaching or student learning. Equal-system weighted latent class analysis examined eight purposes. Adjusted three-step models related AI-related professional learning to profile membership while accounting for classification uncertainty and teacher characteristics. Results and Conclusions: A four-profile solution was retained: preparation-focused (40.07%), design-and-adaptation-focused (23.87%), data-and-feedback-focused (18.70%), and broad-purpose use (17.37%). Beyond breadth, the two intermediate profiles covered a similar range of purposes but diverged in material adaptation and student-data review. Among professional-learning participants, AI-related rather than non-AI content was associated with higher odds of design-and-adaptation membership (OR = 2.03, 95% CI [1.62, 2.53]) and broad-purpose membership (OR = 2.40, 95% CI [1.99, 2.89]) relative to data-and-feedback membership; broad-purpose and design-and-adaptation membership did not differ significantly. Teacher AI use therefore varies in both breadth and instructional purpose. The findings move beyond overall prevalence and provide a task-based basis for designing and evaluating AI-related professional learning, while leaving its effects on teachers’ practice to be tested longitudinally. Manuscript status Under review at the Journal of Computer Assisted Learning. Registration timing This record documents a completed study. Data analysis and manuscript preparation were completed before this registration, and the manuscript is currently under journal review. This is a retrospective registration, not a prospective preregistration.

items.title: Pedagogical Practices and Reflections on AI-Enhanced Innovation in Sustainability Education: Guiding AI Integration Through the IDEA Framework
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence is increasingly influencing sustainability education by providing dynamic tools that foster systems thinking, data literacy, ethical reasoning, and creative problem solving. Yet despite growing experimentation with AI in teaching and learning, there remains a notable gap in practice-based frameworks that guide educators in integrating AI into ESD in ethically grounded and pedagogically purposeful ways. Addressing this need, this chapter explores how AI can be thoughtfully integrated into Education for Sustainable Development (ESD) through innovative pedagogical approaches. Drawing on teaching cases and reflective analysis, it introduces the IDEA (Innovation, Design, Evaluation, and Anchoring) framework as a structured yet flexible guide for integrating AI into practice. The framework is illustrated through practice-informed vignettes, including the use of generative AI for futures thinking, machine learning for environmental data analysis, AI-powered feedback in ethics debates, and co-designed projects with pre-service teachers. These examples highlight both the affordances and tensions of using AI in higher education and teacher preparation programs. The IDEA framework encourages educators to critically examine how AI tools align with sustainability goals, support meaningful learning outcomes, and surface issues of ethics, equity, and digital competence. Situating AI not as a disruptive novelty but as a pedagogical mediator, the chapter contributes to the discourse on ESD and the responsible integration of emerging technologies. Drawing on interdisciplinary scholarship, it reflects on implications for curriculum design, faculty development, and education policy, offering actionable recommendations for creating ethical, inclusive, and future-facing learning environments.

items.abstract: This study was initiated by the uneven learning motivation among junior high school students in Coding and Artificial Intelligence (CAI) subjects. The research aims to enhance students’ learning motivation through a project-based gamification strategy. The method employed was Classroom Action Research (CAR) based on the Kemmis and McTaggart model, conducted in two cycles with 31 students as subjects. The learning process implemented Project-Based Learning (PjBL) integrated with six gamification elements (clear goals, points, challenges, badges, feedback, and leaderboards) through a simple Scratch game development project. Data were collected using an adapted Motivated Strategies for Learning Questionnaire (MSLQ), observations, field notes, and documentation, and analyzed descriptively. The results showed an increase in students’ learning motivation, with the classical average rising from 3.06 (76.39%) in the pre-cycle to 3.24 (81.00%) in Cycle I and 3.38 (84.39%) in Cycle II, and all motivation aspects improving. Students reaching the minimum “High” criterion (score ≥ 3.00) increased from 51.61% (16 students) in the pre-cycle to 77.42% (24 students) in Cycle I, and reached the classical success target at 80.65% (25 students) in Cycle II. In Cycle II, a layered troubleshooting strategy using a Generative AI chatbot as a coding assistant, followed by peer feedback, appeared to support more persistent and independent problem-solving, although the gains were moderate and uneven across students, and self-regulation remained the lowest-scoring aspect (3.09). In conclusion, project-based gamification was accompanied by an increase in junior high school students’ learning motivation in CAI subjects.

items.abstract: Penelitian ini dilatarbelakangi oleh penerapan model pembelajarn Discovery Learning yang belum terlaksana secara optimal, serta penggunaan Artificial Intelligence dalam pembelajaran yang masih bersifat umum, belum terarah, dan belum dimanfaatkan secara inovatif sebagai pendukung proses belajar peserta didik. Kondisi tersebut menyebabkan peserta didik masih mengalami kesulitan dalam memahami konsep-konsep kimia yang bersifat abstrak. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui pengaruh penerapan model Discovery Learning berbantuan Artificial Intelligence terhadap hasil belajar peserta didik pada materi teori asam basa. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan metode pre-experimental design dan desain One Group Pretest-Posttest Design. items.title: PENGARUH MINDFULNESS DAN AILESSPHOBIA TERHADAP EFIKASI DIRI AKADEMIK MAHASISWA SEMESTER AWAL PSIKOLOGI UNESA
items.abstract: The rapid development of generative artificial intelligence in the academic world has triggered a new psychological phenomenon known as ailessphobia, defined as anxiety resulting from the loss of access to AI, whose main dimensions are closely related to academic self-efficacy. Nevertheless, empirical evidence regarding the relationship between ailessphobia and academic self-efficacy still demonstrates inconsistent results, whereas self-efficacy itself is a crucial predictor of first-year students' academic adaptation and achievement success. On the other hand, mindfulness is identified as a protective psychological resource that is positively associated with enhanced self-regulation and self-efficacy among students, making it potential to be tested jointly within a single model. Most prior literature regarding these variables remains dominated by engineering and nursing students abroad. Consequently, studies exploring the effect of mindfulness and ailessphobia on academic self-efficacy among Psychology students in Indonesia, specifically at Universitas Negeri Surabaya, have not yet been found. Given that early-semester students are in a crucial transitional period of self-efficacy development, coupled with the availability of locally validated measurement instruments, conducting this study is essential to fill the void in the literature. This study aims to determine and explain the effect of mindfulness and ailessphobia on students' self-efficacy. The focus of this research is to explore whether mindfulness affects students' academic self-efficacy, as well as whether ailessphobia also influences academic self-efficacy. In addition, this study seeks to ascertain whether both factors (mindfulness & ailessphobia) collectively exert a significant influence on students' academic self-efficacy. The objectives of this research are clearly formulated and measurable, as they directly address the proposed problems and can be tested through quantitative research methods. Hyphotheses : Null Hypothesis (H0): Mindfulness and ailessphobia together do not affect academic self-efficacy among early-semester psychology students at UNESA. Alternative Hypothesis (H1): Mindfulness and ailessphobia affect academic self-efficacy among early-semester psychology students at UNESA. Alternative Hypothesis (H2): Mindfulness affects academic self-efficacy among early-semester psychology students at UNESA. Alternative Hypothesis (H3): Ailessphobia affects academic self-efficacy among early-semester psychology students at UNESA. This study is designed using a quantitative approach with a predictive correlational (explanatory) design. This approach was chosen because it aims to explain and measure the extent to which the independent variables, mindfulness (X1) and ailessphobia (X2), are capable of predicting variations in the dependent variable, namely academic self-efficacy ($Y$). Data were collected using a cross-sectional method, in which data collection was conducted within a single timeframe (a one-shot study) via an online questionnaire hosted on PsyToolkit. The cross-sectional approach provides an empirical overview of the relationships between variables without intervening in or manipulating the respondents' conditions, and it is not intended to infer long-term causal relationships. The target population in this study comprises active undergraduate students in the Psychology Department at Universitas Negeri Surabaya (UNESA) who are in the early transition period of higher education (semesters 1 to 4) and have experience using Generative AI technology for academic activities. Inclusion Criteria: -Active undergraduate Psychology students at UNESA in semesters 1 to 4. -Have utilized Generative AI platforms (such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, or DeepSeek) to complete assignments or academic activities. -Willing to participate and complete the questionnaire voluntarily (informed consent). Exclusion Criteria: -Respondents with incomplete submission data (missing data). -Respondents exhibiting invalid response patterns (e.g., straight-lining or careless responding). -Duplicate submission data. -Students who were involved in the trial phase (try-out) of the research instruments. Academic Self-Efficacy is measured using The Indonesian Academic Self-Efficacy Scale (TIASS) developed by Darmayanti et al. (2024), based on the theoretical framework of Zajacova et al. (2005). This scale consists of 20 positively phrased items. It measures four main dimensions: (1) Interaction at university, (2) Performance out of class, (3) Performance in class, and (4) Managing work, family, and university. Mindfulness is measured using the Short Version of the Five Facet Mindfulness Questionnaire (FFMQ), adapted by Fourianalistyawati et al. (2023). This scale consists of 10 items (6 favorable items and 4 unfavorable items). It encompasses five facets: (1) Observing, (2) Describing, (3) Acting with awareness, (4) Non-judging of inner experience, and (5) Non-reactivity to inner experience. Ailessphobia is measured using the Ailessphobia in Education Scale (AILPES), developed by Gezgin and Türk Kurtça (2025) and translated into Indonesian through translation procedures. This scale consists of 18 items (favorable). It comprises two main factors: (1) Academic self-efficacy anxiety and (2) Lack of academic confidence without AI.

Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan jenis penelitian eksplanatori. Data dikumpulkan melalui kuesioner, observasi, dan dokumentasi, kemudian dianalisis menggunakan metode Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) dengan bantuan perangkat lunak SmartPLS. items.title: Performance of Naïve Spectral Geometric Models in Histopathology AI
items.abstract: Abstract Spectral geometric methods provide mathematically interpretable representations of tissue morphology, yet their standalone performance in histopathology artificial intelligence has not been systematically evaluated. This study benchmarks purely spectral pipelines across representative digital pathology and spatial omics tasks relative to convolutional baselines. Spectral features derived from graph Laplacians, heat kernel signatures, spectral wavelet energy, Slepian concentrations, fractal descriptors, and persistent homology were extracted from histopathology patches using fixed-grid graphs. Features were processed using spectral neural operators and gradient boosting. Four tasks were evaluated: binary breast cancer classification (BreaKHis), multi-class glioblastoma region-patch classification, spatial transcriptomics prediction (10× Visium), and spot-wise denoising. Cross-validation and leave-one-slide-out strategies were applied. Metrics included accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), mean squared error, and Pearson correlation. Equivalence between spectral and CNN models was not established within the prespecified ±0.03 AUC margin. Purely spectral models achieved lower performance than convolutional baselines, with AUC differences of 0.12–0.23. The CNN→LGBM model achieved an accuracy of 0.83 ± 0.06, balanced accuracy of 0.73 ± 0.10, and AUC of 0.80 ± 0.13. Equivalence was not established within the prespecified margin. Fusion achieved balanced accuracy of 0.73 ± 0.08, equal to the CNN baseline mean balanced accuracy, without surpassing CNN AUC. Spatial transcriptomics prediction showed limited cross-slide generalization (Pearson correlation 0.06), whereas spot-wise denoising under sparse conditions showed competitive performance. Spectral geometric models do not outperform convolutional methods for classification or segmentation but provide complementary utility in denoising and sparse spatial settings.

items.title: Permission to Retry: A Study of Authorization and Recovery in AI Agent Workflows
items.abstract: A durable agent can resume a consequential action while its authority changes and the action's external outcome remains uncertain. We study execution-time reliability of tool-using AI agents, isolating recovery decisions from language-model behavior. Checkpoint state, permission to dispatch, evidence of an external effect and permission to reconcile are distinct obligations. We present a finite conformance study that checks these obligations through histories scored against a provider effect ledger hidden from the recovering application. A prospectively frozen campaign executes 336 histories on native LangGraph and Temporal hosts, crossing 14 schedules, three provider contracts and four matched application policies. All 168 paired host cells have identical checked outcomes. Per host, retained-ledger reconciliation passes all 42 histories: 21 checked completions, 15 denials and six unknown outcomes with reservations retained. Cached retry, revalidation before retry and stable-key retry pass 30, 36 and 31 histories respectively. A separate 16-case component study of InfinityOS, an enterprise AI platform developed by Arya.ai, exercises exported authority, worker, recovery and settlement code over repository fakes. The results isolate the roles of current authority, provider contracts and retained observations in recovery, with safety, completion and unresolved obligations reported separately for the declared application profile.

items.title: Phronix: The Capability-Centric Learning Paradigm for Agents
items.abstract: Scientific computing increasingly relies on large language model-based agents for performance engineering tasks such as instrumentation, analysis, and workflow porting. However, agent effectiveness depends heavily on the surrounding harness, which typically relies on manually written skills and curated memory. This limits autonomous learning, forcing agents to repeatedly rediscover solutions rather than retain and reuse knowledge from prior executions. We introduce Phronix, a capability-centric learning paradigm that enables agentic harnesses to acquire, validate, and refine reusable capabilities from their own executions. Phronix operates through a predictor-validator-corrector loop: MCP tools and associated skills propose solutions, tool executions validate them, and observed outcomes refine the stored capabilities. It distills every observed interaction into a capability store and researches a failing task rather than abandoning it. First, such learned capabilities solve a recurring task on the first attempt in 93-95% of cases across every model, significantly reducing solution non-determinism and improving reliability. Second, Phronix turns an agent's own execution into 7.6-30.8 durable capabilities per task without user instruction, and creation falls below two once the needed capability exists. Third, warm-start runs consume only 0.38-0.40 million tokens per task, which is three to four times less than a single baseline attempt, while a cold-start costs no more than the baseline. On the 1000 Genome Pegasus workflow, instrumenting a production application for I/O performance analysis, Phronix passes all 11 correctness checks against six for the baseline harness, and also lifts the task solving rates of two cheaper models from 29% and 27% of SWE-bench tasks solved to 91% and 87%, respectively, matching the performance of the most expensive evaluated model.

items.title: Physical and Mental Health Consequences of Work-Related Stress: A Comparative Study of Women and Men
items.abstract: Work-related stress is a leading occupational health concern, and a substantial literature suggests its consequences differ between women and men. Most of that literature, however, establishes that a difference exists without identifying the mechanism responsible. This study examined the physical and mental health consequences of work-related stress among employed women and men, and tested whether differences persisted after psychosocial working conditions were controlled. A comparative cross-sectional design was adopted. Data were collected from 101 full-time employees aged 25-50 in Bengaluru, India; the analytical sample comprised 100 participants (50 women, 50 men). A 50-item instrument assessed perceived stress, working conditions, physical symptoms, emotional wellbeing and coping. Physical health and emotional wellbeing scales showed good reliability (alpha = .83 and .86). Five of six hypotheses were unsupported: women and men did not differ in perceived stress (p = .584, d = -0.11), physical symptoms (p = .986, d = 0.004) or emotional wellbeing (p = .575, d = 0.11), and gender did not moderate the stress-health relationship. One significant difference emerged: men reported greater problem-focused coping (p < .001, d = -0.73), although the predicted difference in emotion-focused coping did not appear. Perceived stress correlated strongly with physical symptoms (r = .55) and emotional wellbeing (r = .62), explaining 30% and 39% of variance. Findings are consistent with a differential-exposure account: where working conditions were comparable, health consequences were comparable.

items.title: PIU Smart Intelligence Agents: Design and Implementation of a Security-Aware Multi-Agent Architecture for Enterprise Intelligence
items.abstract: Enterprises increasingly rely on heterogeneous documents, relational databases, and analytical systems to support information retrieval and business decision-making. Integrating large language models (LLMs) with these sources introduces challenges in evidence reliability, analytical correctness, access control, and operational resilience. This paper presents PIU Smart Intelligence Agents, a security-aware multi-agent architecture designed to integrate enterprise document intelligence, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), semantic search, document summarization, naturallanguage-to-SQL analytics, key performance indicator (KPI) generation, and conversational AI within a common application and governance framework. The proposed architecture organizes specialized AI capabilities around shared services for authentication, authorization, request validation, provider integration, observability, and controlled data access. Its document-processing workflow encompasses file validation, text extraction, optical character recognition for scanned documents, normalization, chunking, embedding generation, and vector-based indexing. The structured-analytics workflow separates schema-aware query generation from SQL validation, restricted database execution, and result interpretation. The architecture also addresses provider compatibility, timeout handling, failure recovery, document lifecycle management, and traceability of generated outputs. The source implementation reports 1,242 automated tests passed and two integration tests skipped. These results are reported implementation evidence and have not been independently reproduced. The available evidence does not establish comprehensive external RAG benchmark performance, quantitative correctness across all agents, independently validated security effectiveness, or production-scale performance and recovery guarantees. Accordingly, this study presents an integrated engineering architecture and identifies a reproducible evaluation framework for assessing its effectiveness. The principal contribution is the systematic integration of heterogeneous enterprise AI capabilities with explicit governance and validation requirements, rather than the introduction of a new learning or retrieval algorithm. Future work should prioritize agent-specific correctness testing, retrieval and answer-quality benchmarks, adversarial security evaluation, controlled load testing, and recovery verification.

items.title: Pixels to precision: Deep learning in dental imaging
items.abstract: Dental imaging is fundamental to diagnosis, treatment planning, and follow-up in Oral Medicine and Maxillofacial Radiology. Although conventional radiographic interpretation remains dependent on professional expertise, diagnostic performance may be influenced by observer variability, image quality, workload, and the subtle nature of early pathological changes. The development of Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly deep learning (DL), has introduced new approaches for automated analysis of dental and maxillofacial images. This narrative review discusses the evolution, principles, applications, clinical relevance, limitations, and future directions of deep learning in dental imaging, with emphasis on intraoral radiography, panoramic radiography, cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT), and related imaging modalities. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have demonstrated applications in dental caries detection, periodontal bone assessment, periapical lesion detection, tooth identification and numbering, jaw lesion analysis, anatomical segmentation, and treatment planning. More advanced architectures, including U-Net, residual networks, object-detection models, three-dimensional CNNs, and emerging transformer-based systems, have expanded the scope of automated image interpretation. However, the rapid growth of research has also highlighted important limitations, including small and heterogeneous datasets, inconsistent annotation, retrospective study designs, limited external validation, algorithmic bias, and difficulties in explaining model predictions. Importantly, high algorithmic accuracy does not necessarily translate into clinical effectiveness. Future research should therefore focus on diverse multicentre datasets, external and prospective validation, explainable AI, multimodal systems, ethical governance, and meaningful human-AI collaboration. Deep learning is most appropriately viewed as an adjunctive clinical decision-support technology that complements rather than replaces professional diagnostic judgment.

items.title: PlaceIntel: A Multi-Agentic AI-Powered Campus Placement Management and Preparation Platform
items.abstract: Abstract— Preparing students for campus recruitment in a personalized and effective way is still difficult for most colleges. Typical placement systems deal mainly with administrative work such as registering students, storing company details, checking eligibility, and organizing recruitment drives, whereas interview training and companyspecific preparation are usually left to separate resources. This paper describes PlaceIntel, a web platform driven by multiple cooperating AI agents that unites central placement administration with tailored AI support for students. Four dedicated agents form the core of the system: a Mock Interview Agent, a Company Preparation Agent, a Company Research Agent, and a Skill Gap Analyzer. A Candidate Evaluation module additionally supports structured assessment during placement drives. The implementation relies on React, Java Spring Boot, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, Redis, LangGraph, and Gemini 3.6 Flash; authentication is handled with Spring Security and JWT, while Docker and AWS are used for deployment. The resulting architecture brings placement operations and AI-guided preparationtogether within a single modular design.

items.title: PointerBench: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Fine-Grained GUI Grounding
items.abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models have shown promising performance in computer-use tasks, from planning user workflows to grounding natural-language actions to precise UI targets. Existing end-to-end benchmarks primarily emphasize long-horizon task completion, while GUI grounding benchmarks remain focused on conventional controls and a limited set of professional interfaces. We introduce POINTERBENCH, a diagnostic suite of 1,500 screenshot-instruction pairs probing three complementary capabilities: thin sub-element identification and geometric grounding in spreadsheets (POINTERBENCH-Sheets), character-level grounding in long-text documents (POINTERBENCH-Text), and mixed GUI grounding across 100 professional applications (POINTERBENCH-Pro). We carefully curate each task with pixel-exact target geometry and evaluate both general-purpose multimodal models and 39 specialist GUI grounding configurations. We find text grounding to be the most challenging setting, with Claude Fable 5, GPT-5.6 Sol, and the leading native specialist UI-Venus-2-9B achieving 69.6%, 53.4%, and 25.8% success on POINTERBENCH-Text despite respective 83.2%, 77.7%, and 54.5% average success across POINTERBENCH. These results reveal substantial headroom in fine-grained GUI grounding across frontier and specialist models. We publicly release the benchmark and evaluation code at https://github.com/warmwindOS/pointerbench.

items.title: Pondus: an agentic structural analysis and design program built on the Stabileo engine
items.abstract: Language-model agents can now operate engineering programs through tool interfaces, but a structuralprogram that an agent drives has to be designed for that user, because the agent accepts whatever numbersthe tools return. This paper describes Pondus, an open-source native program in which a language-modelagent and an engineer work on one three-dimensional structural model, and reports how it is built, howit is used and how far its results can be trusted. The agent reaches the program through a Model ContextProtocol server of 44 tools, either from the chat panel of the desktop application, where a vendored agentharness runs one agent session per message on a copy of the model, or from external agents such asClaude Desktop and ChatGPT. Every tool calls the same functions as the engineer’s interface, so a modelbuilt by the agent can be checked, edited and undone by hand. The analysis runs on the Stabileo engine,which Pondus links as a library with four marked changes: Pondus splits members, transfers slab loads,generates shear walls as wide columns with rigid arms and builds the seismic mass before handing asolver input to the engine, and it designs to ACI 318-19, AISC 360-16 and EN 1993-1-1 from the results.Two agent runs with a low-cost model built, analysed and designed a two-storey frame in 105 s with 13tool calls and a five-storey frame with shear walls under an ASCE 7-22 response spectrum, including a16-page calculation report, in 382 s with 22 tool calls. Every number in the agent’s answers matched thetools and hand checks of the loads, the seismic weight and the base shear, but the answers also containedfour descriptive errors, such as reporting two deepened beams where the program had deepened six, andthey did not point out that the walls resist load only in one direction, so the response modification factorof the walls was applied to the frame direction as well. A calibration against 470 published, closed-formand independent reference values over 229 cases found 430 within 0.5 % and 449 within 1 %, and it foundfourteen defects, thirteen of them in the code that prepares the inputs of the engine and the design checksrather than in the numerical kernels. Together these results suggest that the tools of an agentic structuralprogram can be made accurate, whereas the agent’s prose remains the weaker link that the engineer mustread against the program’s own tables.

items.title: Potential Future Shifts in Television Production in Light of Technological Development
items.abstract: This research aims to anticipate potential future transformations in the television production industry amidst rapid technological advancements and to examine their impact on production quality and the efficiency of technical and professional processes. It also seeks to identify the key challenges media organizations face in adopting and integrating modern technologies into television production environments. The study focuses on three main areas: the role of modern technologies in enhancing television production quality; the technical, human, economic, and organizational challenges associated with their adoption; and the impact of artificial intelligence applications—a prominent feature of contemporary technological transformation—on production process efficiency. The study employed a descriptive methodology, utilizing a questionnaire to gather data from a sample of 400 participants—professionals and staff within the radio and television sectors. The sample encompassed broadcasters, directors, editors, producers, engineers, technicians, media researchers, and marketing and advertising personnel, as well as channel and station managers and consultants in technology and IT. This approach enabled an examination of diverse professional perspectives regarding the current state of technological transformations and their potential future trends. The research findings indicate that modern technological advancements—particularly artificial intelligence applications—play a significant role in evolving television production processes. This is achieved by enhancing audio and visual quality, developing visual effects, improving content management efficiency, automating certain operational tasks, and minimizing human error. Conversely, the results reveal a number of challenges that could hinder the adoption of these technologies, most notably high costs and the need to upgrade the professional and technical skills of the workforce. In light of these findings, the research discusses potential future transformations in the television production industry—specifically the shift toward smarter, more flexible production environments, the reshaping of certain professional roles, and the increasing reliance on advanced technical solutions across various stages of production.

items.title: Precision Cardiovascular Medicine: Integrating Pharmacogenomics, Biomarkers, Artificial Intelligence, and Real-World Evidence
items.abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains a major global cause of morbidity and mortality, with substantial interindividual variation in disease risk, treatment response, and susceptibility to adverse effects. Precision cardiovascular medicine incorporates patient-level information to refine cardiovascular prevention, diagnosis, risk stratification, and treatment. This structured narrative review is based on a structured literature search, with 213 publications included in the synthesis. This review synthesizes evidence on four complementary domains: pharmacogenomics, biomarkers, artificial intelligence (AI), and real-world evidence (RWE), and examines their potential integration in cardiovascular care. Pharmacogenomics has established applications in selected gene–drug pairs, including CYP2C19–clopidogrel, CYP2C9/VKORC1–warfarin, and SLCO1B1–statin-associated muscle toxicity, although implementation varies according to evidence, accessibility, and clinical infrastructure. Biomarker research extends beyond cardiac troponins to markers of myocardial stress, fibrosis, inflammation, and molecular regulation, including soluble ST2, galectin-3, GDF-15, and microRNAs. AI and machine learning provide approaches for analyzing multimodal cardiovascular data and have been investigated for risk assessment, phenotyping, imaging, ECG analysis, and clinical decision support. RWE complements randomized evidence by providing information on treatment utilization, safety, effectiveness, and outcomes in routine-care populations, while challenges include data quality, confounding, and incomplete ascertainment. Across coronary artery disease, heart failure, atrial fibrillation, hypertension, dyslipidemia, and inherited cardiovascular diseases, increasing opportunities exist to integrate these domains. However, clinical translation remains influenced by validation, interpretability, generalizability, cost, regulation, data governance, and health equity. Future research should emphasize prospective evaluation, diverse-population validation, interoperable infrastructure, and assessment of clinical utility to support the responsible integration of precision approaches into cardiovascular care.

items.title: Predicting acute intracranial vascular events in stroke alerts using large-language models and structured data
items.abstract: Acute stroke alerts are frequently activated for non-cerebrovascular conditions, creating false positives that strain resources and increase diagnostic uncertainty. We developed machine learning models integrating large-language models, structured electronic health record data, and clinical time-series features to predict acute intracranial vascular event (AIVE) at stroke alert activation. Using retrospective stroke alerts from the Mount Sinai Health System (2011–2021), we extracted demographics, comorbidities, medications, vital signs, laboratory results, and clinical notes documented before alert activation. AIVE was defined using radiographic gold standards as a composite of acute cerebrovascular and selected acute intracranial diagnoses. Notes were modeled using Clinical-Longformer, MxBAI embeddings with a feed-forward neural network, and BioWordVec embeddings with logistic regression; structured-data models used complementary hyperparameter-tuned workflows. Model outputs were combined in a late-fusion stacked ensemble and evaluated on internal and within-system held-out hospital test sets. Among 16,512 stroke alerts, 9,013 (55.6%) were due to AIVE. The multimodal model achieved an AUROC of 0.73 (95% CI, 0.71–0.75), positive predictive value of 0.68, sensitivity of 0.76, F1-score of 0.72, and specificity of 0.56 on internal testing, with similar held-out hospital performance. This approach may support post-activation stroke-alert risk stratification and reduce false-positive evaluations.

items.title: Predicting Music Valence and Arousal via Textual and Multimodal In-Context Learning in Large Language Models
items.abstract: While arousal can be reliably predicted from musical audio, emotional valence remains difficult to model due to its subjective and context-dependent nature. In this work, we investigate the potential of in-context learning (ICL) with large language models to advance continuous valence and arousal prediction. Rather than predicting emotion scores directly, our framework leverages contextual demonstrations from an auxiliary dataset to refine the initial predictions produced by a small, task-specific base model. We systematically evaluate a text-based ICL variant using lyrics and generated audio captions, alongside a multimodal variant that incorporates raw audio signals. Using the entire MER60 dataset strictly as a held-out test set, our experiments demonstrate substantial performance gains, particularly for valence. Text-based ICL improves the valence $R^2$ from 0.110 to 0.427 with 80 demonstration shots, while the multimodal variant achieves 0.346 with only 10 shots. These findings suggest that training-free ICL offers an effective inference-time strategy for current language models to predict continuous music emotion.

items.title: Predictive Analytics for Supply Chain Resilience and Logistics Optimisation in Volatile Operating Environments
items.abstract: Introduction: Volatile operating environments create demand uncertainty, supplier disruptions, delivery delays, geopolitical shocks, and other events that can negatively affect operational performance and supply chain resilience. Evidence on the contribution of predictive analytics to both logistics optimisation and resilience is still fragmented, and opportunities exist to anticipate these risks and inform timely logistics decision-making. This systematic review aims to collate evidence on the use of predictive analytics to improve supply chain resilience and optimise logistics operations in volatile operating environments, with a specific focus on predictive techniques, applications, outcomes, and implementation challenges. Methods: A systematic literature review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020. Terms relating to predictive analytics, supply chains and logistics, resilience and risk, and optimisation were used to search Scopus and the Web of Science Core Collection. Eligible studies applied machine learning, deep learning, artificial intelligence (AI)-based predictive modelling, or related forecasting approaches to problems involving uncertainty, disruption, risk, resilience, or optimisation in supply-chain and/or logistics settings. After deduplication, 321 unique records were screened by title and abstract; 30 reports underwent full-text assessment, and 15 studies were included in the synthesis. Results: The 15 included studies showed substantial methodological and contextual heterogeneity. Applications concentrated on demand forecasting, inventory management, supplier risk, disruption prediction, and product availability. Methods included ensemble learning, deep learning, hybrid models, and adaptive approaches. Predictive performance often improved relative to study-specific comparators, although greater model complexity did not consistently produce better performance. The clearest operational gains were reported when predictions were coupled with optimisation or decision-support processes such as inventory allocation, replenishment, and supplier selection. Evidence relevant to resilience was strongest for anticipation, visibility, response, and recovery, whereas direct evidence for longer-term adaptation remained limited. Common implementation constraints included data quality, data availability, model adaptability, interpretability, and organisational infrastructure. Conclusion: Predictive analytics can support supply-chain resilience and logistics performance when predictive outputs are translated into timely operational decisions. The evidence remains heterogeneous and context-dependent; future research should prioritise external validation, longitudinal assessment, and direct measurement of resilience outcomes.

items.title: Predictive Underground Water Leakage Detection Using Artificial Intelligence and the Internet of Things
items.abstract: Unaccounted-for water loss resulting from undetected underground pipe leaks poses a persistent operational and financial challenge for municipal distribution systems worldwide. In conventional utility practice, leaks are predominantly identified reactively—either when water eventually breaches the surface or following localized pressure drop complaints from consumers. In this paper, we develop a proactive, multi-sensor predictive leakage detection framework that pairs a low-power edge Internet of Things (IoT) architecture with a hybrid machine learning pipeline. Subsurface pipe segments are monitored using five complementary sensing modalities: hydraulic pressure, inline flow velocity, pipe-wall structural vibration via a MEMS accelerometer, soil moisture, and ambient temperature. Sensor readings are acquired, pre-filtered, and transmitted by an energy-efficient ESP32-based edge node using LoRa wireless communication and TLS-secured MQTT to a central analytics backend. A sliding-window feature extraction stage derives short-term statistical trends and feeds an unsupervised Isolation Forest model; the resulting anomaly metric is concatenated with temporal features to train a gradient boosting classifier that forecasts the likelihood of a leak initiating within a two-hour predictive lead window (H = 12 steps). We evaluate the proposed approach on a synthetic distribution network of 60 pipe segments that explicitly incorporates gradual, incipient mechanical degradation prior to burst onset. Benchmarked against a conventional static pressure threshold (F1 = 0.830) and standard supervised classifiers, the proposed hybrid model achieves an F1-score of 0.992 and provides a median warning lead time of 1.9 hours (mean 1.8 hours) ahead of physical rupture, with zero false alarms and zero missed events across held-out test segments. Finally, we analyze model sensitivity across noise regimes and establish key deployment requirements for district metered area field implementations.

items.title: Present, Yet Unseen: Investigating OSF Search Omissions, Recovery, and Institutional Connections
items.abstract: Public research depends on being discoverable. This investigation documents a failure in that basic function: two public OSF registrations—The Irreversible Constraint Regime and The Life Equation—were accessible through their direct records but absent from the registration-search results tested. The preserved evidence records a concrete discrepancy. The public contributor API listed 21 registrations, while the corresponding search returned 19, omitting these two works. Their records identified them as public, accepted, unembargoed, and not withdrawn. Stored metadata cards contained their titles, identifiers, and authorship, yet the documented searches failed to retrieve them. The investigation preserves screenshots, exact API responses, timestamps, correspondence, and cryptographic integrity hashes so that these observations can be independently examined. Following the author’s inquiry, discoverability was restored. OSF Support confirmed a manual SHARE re-index and subsequently stated that it had re-indexed the public content at the author’s request. items.title: Prevalence and functional impact of musculoskeletal pain among university students in seven Arab countries and its sociodemographic and lifestyle associations
items.abstract: Musculoskeletal pain (MSP) represents a major public health challenge globally, particularly among university students who are in a critical transitional phase of life characterized by intense academic demands, lifestyle changes, and increasing reliance on digital technologies. Sedentary behavior (SB) has been identified as a potential risk factor for MSP; however, evidence from the Arab region remains limited. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of MSP in nine body regions (neck, shoulders, upper back, elbows, wrists/hands, lower back, hips/thighs, knees, and ankles/feet) across four time points (lifetime, past 12 months, past month, and today), to assess the impact of MSP, and examine the association between SB and MSP. A multinational cross-sectional study was conducted among 4300 university students in seven Arab countries (Egypt, Yemen, Iraq, Sudan, Jordan, Syria, and Palestine), using an online Arabic self-administered questionnaire. Convenience and snowball sampling methods were used to recruit eligible study respondents. MSP was assessed using the Arabic version of the Extended Nordic Musculoskeletal Questionnaire (NMQ-E). SB was assessed using sedentary behavior questionnaire (SBQ). Chi-square tests were used for univariate associations. Binary logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with any MSP in the past 12 months, and to identify predictors of high SB. Adjusted odds ratios (aOR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were reported, and a p-value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. The prevalence of MSP in at least one body region was 84.0% (lifetime), 71.3% (past 12 months), and 64.9% (past month). The neck (49.3%) and lower back (37.3%) were the most affected regions in the past 12 months. Among those affected, preventing usual activities (range: 48.8%–71.7%) and taking medication (range: 37.6–48.2%) were the most reported impacts, while hospitalization remained relatively low (3.2–14.2%). Female sex (aOR = 1.98, 95% CI 1.69–2.31), chronic diseases (aOR = 1.90, 95% CI 1.44–2.49), MSP family history (aOR = 1.96, 95% CI 1.56–2.47), moderate SB (aOR = 1.56, 95% CI 1.32–1.84), and high SB (aOR = 1.42, 95% CI 1.16–1.72) were significantly associated with MSP in the past 12 months, while sleeping 6–8 h was protective (aOR = 0.79, 95% CI 0.67–0.92). This study found a high prevalence of MSP among university students in Arab countries, particularly affecting the neck and lower back. Higher SB, chronic diseases, and a family history of MSP were associated with MSP, whereas adequate sleep appeared to be protective. These findings support the need for university-based strategies that reduce prolonged SB and promote musculoskeletal health, including ergonomic education, active breaks, adjustable study stations, and more active learning environments.

items.title: Prevalence of and factors associated with low back pain among construction workers in Mogadishu, Somalia
items.abstract: Background Low back pain (LBP) is a leading cause of disability, particularly in labor-intensive industries. While biomechanical hazards are well-documented in developed nations, epidemiological data from unregulated construction sectors in post-conflict regions remains extremely scarce. This study aimed to estimate the prevalence and identify factors associated with LBP among manual construction workers in Mogadishu, Somalia. Methods An analytic cross-sectional study was conducted among 191 manual workers recruited via stratified random sampling from five major construction companies. Data were collected using a culturally-adapted Nordic Musculoskeletal Questionnaire to assess socio-demographic, lifestyle, and occupational exposures. We utilized a multivariable mixed-effects logistic regression model, accounting for clustering by company, to identify independent associated factors. Results are reported as adjusted odds ratios (AOR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI). Results The workforce was notably young (median age = 26 years), registering an LBP period prevalence of 51.9% (95% CI: 43.5–60.3%). In the adjusted analysis, income status was the strongest predictor, with workers living below extreme poverty facing elevated odds of LBP (AOR = 7.60; 95% CI: 2.48–23.28). Other factors significantly associated included possessing over six years of work experience (AOR = 4.85; 95% CI: 1.56–15.11), being underweight (AOR = 5.22; 95% CI: 1.24–21.94), tobacco use (AOR = 5.70; 95% CI: 1.94–16.78), and inadequate sleep duration of fewer than six hours (AOR = 4.11; 95% CI: 1.28–13.24). Biomechanically, frequency of heavy lifting (AOR = 4.29; 95% CI: 1.26–14.56) and bending (AOR = 5.35; 95% CI: 1.33–21.45) were strongly associated with reporting LBP. Conclusion LBP is highly prevalent among construction workers in Mogadishu. The factors associated with LBP were extreme poverty, inadequate physiological tissue recovery, and severe biomechanical overload. Mitigating this crisis requires site-level ergonomic interventions, such as team-lifting protocols, alongside overarching policies that establish baseline wages to address foundational socioeconomic hazards.

items.title: Privacy Concerns, Perceived Privacy Control, and Trust in Google Digital Services: Evidence on Continued Use Intention among Young Users in Bangladesh
items.abstract: The expansion of Google digital services and the growing integration of generative artificial intelligence have intensified the importance of privacy, user control, and trust in digital-service relationships. This study examines whether privacy concern and perceived privacy control are associated with trust in Google digital services and whether these perceptions, together with trust, explain users’ intention to continue using Google/Gemini services in Bangladesh. Drawing on Privacy Calculus Theory and Trust Theory, the study develops a model in which privacy concern is expected to reduce trust, perceived privacy control is expected to strengthen trust, and trust is expected to increase continued-use intention. A quantitative, cross-sectional survey design was applied to the Group 2 Google master dataset. After screening, 385 complete cases were retained, with all retained respondents satisfying the attention-check criterion. Three-item measures captured privacy concern, perceived privacy control, trust, and continued-use intention using a five-point Likert scale. Composite-score regressions with bootstrap inference were used to reproduce the planned SEM/PLSSEM-oriented structural assessment. The results indicate that perceived privacy control positively predicts trust (β = .167, p = .001), whereas privacy concern does not have a statistically significant effect on trust (β = .080, p = .114). Trust is a substantial positive predictor of continued-use intention (β = .347, p < .001), and perceived privacy control also has a positive direct association with continued use (β = .129, p = .007). Privacy concern does not significantly predict continued use (β = .058, p = .217). Bootstrap mediation indicates a significant indirect effect of perceived privacy control through trust, while the privacy-concern indirect effect is not statistically distinguishable from zero. The findings suggest that users’ perceived ability to understand and manage privacy settings may be more consequential for trust and continued use than generalized privacy concern alone. The study contributes Bangladesh-specific evidence to privacy-calculus and trust research and offers practical implications for Google and other digital-service providers seeking to strengthen transparency, user control, and durable trust in the generative-AI era.

items.title: Professional perspectives on sensory and spatial barriers relevant to neuro-inclusive secondary school environments in Nigeria
items.abstract: Introduction Sensory and spatial characteristics of learning environments can influence how neurodivergent students participate in education. This study examined professional accounts of built‐environment barriers relevant to neuro-inclusive secondary‐school design in Nigeria. Methods Seven multidisciplinary professionals were interviewed virtually using a semi‐structured guide. Four had direct experience with secondary‐school‐aged learners, while others worked in therapeutic, special‐needs, rehabilitation, or care/support settings. Open‐ended responses were analysed inductively using reflexive thematic analysis, while responses to nine predefined design features were synthesised separately as prompted feature appraisals. Results Four themes were generated: sensory environmental stressors; environmental distress and spatial dysregulation; restorative and regulatory features; and spatial configuration, transition, and classroom ergonomics. Auditory and visual conditions, crowding, abrupt transitions, and limited retreat space were prominent concerns. Funding, space, institutional readiness, and implementation knowledge affected feasibility. A preliminary three‐tier retrofit framework prioritised acoustic control, lighting control, withdrawal/escape spaces, and sensory zoning (Tier 1); flexible furniture and wayfinding/predictability (Tier 2); and biophilic respite, visual simplification/colour, and temperature/ventilation (Tier 3). Discussion The findings provide mixed‐context professional proxy evidence relevant to Nigerian secondary‐school design. The framework is preliminary and unvalidated and should be tested through co‐design with neurodivergent students and objective environmental assessment.
